e8125211aa169e06: NIBONG TEBAL: Continuous heavy rain triggered flash floods overnight, trapping 16 residents from three families in Kampung Sethu, Sungai Bakap, early today.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations division assistant director John Sagun Francis said firefighters were deployed to the scene following a distress call received at 12.40am.
"Upon arrival, rescuers found several houses submerged under about three feet (0.9m) of floodwaters following persistent downpours.
"Firefighters wearing full personal protective equipment conducted rescue operations using a fibreglass boat to safely evacuate 10 adults and six children.
"The victims were handed over to their relatives who were present at the scene," he said.
He said the floodwaters gradually receded and the operation ended at 2.30am after the area was declared safe.

At 10.32pm yesterday, firefighters were also dispatched to monitor flash flooding at Lorong Jawi Jaya 1, Taman Jawi Jaya, after water levels rose to about 0.3m due to heavy rain and an overflowing nearby river.
No evacuations were required during the incident.
Meanwhile, in a separate incident at 1.10am today, a tree fell onto a residential garage at Kampung Changkat, Sungai Jawi, damaging a parked Perodua Bezza.
John said eight firefighters from the Nibong Tebal fire station were deployed to clear the debris.
"The team carried out cutting and clearing works on the fallen tree.
"No injuries were reported, and the site was handed over to the homeowner after the area was declared safe at 3.35am," he said.

e33534e5ba01eb6e: IPOH, Nov 11 — A total of 48 units of cryptocurrency (bitcoin) mining machines were seized by the police in an operation yesterday at a residential premises in the Seri Iskandar area, which is believed to be the location for the mining activities with illegal electrical wire connections.

Perak Tengah district police chief Supt Hafezul Helmi Hamzah said the raid was conducted by the Criminal Investigation Division of the Perak Tengah district police headquarters (IPD) in collaboration with the Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) engineering team.
“In addition, two units of fast ethernet switches, one Internet router unit, and one cut electrical cable roll were also seized.
“The case is being investigated under Section 427 of the Penal Code and Section 31(1) of the Electricity Supply Act 1990,” he said in a statement last night.

He said the police take the illegal connection of electricity supply for cryptocurrency mining seriously because such actions are against the law, cause losses to utility providers, and increase the risk of fire and public safety.

Therefore, he advised the public not to engage in any illegal activities and requested that any information related to suspected cryptocurrency mining activities involving electricity theft be reported to the police for further action. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Supt is short for Superintendent and IPD means Ibu Pejabat Polis Daerah in Malay.
6386db2f1bc0b7ea: TEHRAN, Nov 11 — Top US diplomat Marco Rubio said yesterday that he saw no need to attack Iran again, as diplomatic efforts to end the war gathered steam and Tehran urged Washington to accept its demands for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
Hours after President Donald Trump said he saw “positive momentum” towards resolving the eight-month war, Rubio said the United States’ squeezing of Iran’s economy made further attacks unnecessary.

“The economic campaign (against Iran) is so devastating that right now there is no need for major combat operations,” the secretary of state said after a meeting of G7 foreign ministers in Paris. “That’s what I told our allies here today.”

Iran’s efforts to blockade Hormuz, the major exit route for Gulf energy shipments, have sent oil prices soaring — a major factor in the humbling of Trump’s Republicans in last week’s midterm elections.

Washington has imposed a counter-blockade on Iranian ports and in August announced what it called an “economic asphyxiation” campaign aimed at financially strangling Iran, already battered by years of sanctions.
Britain’s Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband called for greater efforts to end the conflict, while warning of the economic damage of an ongoing impasse.
“We need to move beyond the ‘no war, no peace’ stalemate, which is causing deep economic pain for our countries,” he said in Paris.
“We must see an all-out diplomatic effort to end this conflict, prevent a nuclear Iran and the threats it poses around the world, and get the Strait of Hormuz properly reopened.”

Washington has appeared to taper down its threats of renewed strikes after the Republicans’ defeat, and even Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu — who launched the war alongside Trump and recently lobbied to “forever eliminate the existential threat of Iran” — appeared to recognise the shifting diplomatic reality.

“In the very near future, we’re going to be confronted by international pressure to accept a nuclear-armed Iran and the preservation of this terror regime that seeks to annihilate us,” he said yesterday.
‘Address Iran’s demands’
Tehran said its offer to reopen Hormuz within two days — if Washington agreed to a raft of conditions — remained on the table.
Iran’s demands have included ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing its assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US blockade of its ports.
“The conflict with Iran will not be resolved through military means, nor by intensifying sanctions,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told the IRNA news agency.
“The only solution is to adopt a language of respect, engage in diplomacy, and address Iran’s demands and conditions — which were outlined in the two-day proposal and remain on the table.”
Meanwhile, vessels continue to come under attack in and around the strait.

The Emirati state oil company ADNOC said yesterday that one of its vessels had “sustained damage following an attack in the UAE’s territorial waters”, while the British maritime agency UKMTO reported a tanker was “struck by an unknown projectile” off the Omani coast.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said that three oil tankers were on fire in the Strait of Hormuz, though it was unclear whether they were referring to the same ships.
US ‘more flexible’ after midterms

On Monday, after meeting Qatar’s prime minister at the White House, Trump said that the US was “locked and loaded”, but further strikes were “quite unlikely” given that key US allies in the Gulf “would prefer the status quo”.
“We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this Conflict, and will ensure that America’s interests are at all times protected,” he wrote on social media.
Qatar and Pakistan are leading diplomatic efforts to resolve the war, which began with US-Israeli strikes that killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in late February.
Qatari foreign ministry official Ibrahim al-Hashmi confirmed there had been progress in the negotiations.
“The mediator is making a persistent and earnest effort to bridge the gaps between the parties’ positions,” he told a regular briefing, adding: “We remain hopeful.”
Iranian political analyst Ali Bigdeli said the outcome of the US elections appeared to have “somewhat reduced Iran’s flexibility, whereas the Americans have become more flexible”.
He noted that the Iranian terms were “demanding and heavy for the United States to accept” but added that “engaging in direct talks” could bear results.
Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei urged Washington to “surrender” to the Iranian demands.
“The war on Iran has already wrecked the US government. But Washington flails like a desperate gambler. FOLD YOUR HAND,” he posted on X. — AFP
f8f8fb061d64888c: SINGAPORE: The dollar held gains near a two-week high in early Asian trade on Wednesday as a hotter-than-expected inflation report and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials fuelled bets the central bank will raise rates next month.
The US dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was steady at 102.22, closing in on its highest level since Oct 28.
The gauge traded up 0.5% on Tuesday after data showed US consumer prices increased by more than expected in October amid higher costs for food and accommodation.

"The rates market isn't simply pricing another hike," said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone Group Ltd in Melbourne. "It's questioning how restrictive US monetary policy may ultimately need to become, and that's a far more consequential debate for risk assets."

The dollar held onto its gains against its major peers in early Asian trade. The euro and the British pound were flat at US$1.1168 and US$1.3345, respectively. Against the yen, the US dollar was unchanged at 158.715 yen. The Australian dollar was up 0.1% at US$0.6870, edging back from a seven-month low, while the New Zealand dollar was flat at US$0.5605.

Comments from voting members of the Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee signalling unease over high inflation have firmed expectations for further rate hikes, prompting traders to all but abandon bets that the US central bank will stand pat at its next policy meeting, which concludes on Dec 9.

Fed funds futures now imply a 91.9% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike next month, up from 84% a day earlier, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool. Markets have fully priced out the possibility of a pause and see a 9.1% chance of a larger 50-basis-point move, while assigning better-than-even odds to a second hike in January.
The yield on the US 10-year Treasury bond was up 13.8 basis points at 4.996%.
In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin was down 0.3% at US$73,566.45 while ether was 0.5% lower at US$2,044.61, both trading near three-month lows.
5ab908a2280392f0: HONG KONG: At 71, Hong Kong superstar Chow Yun Fat is arguably fitter than many people half his age. Affectionately known as "Fat Gor", the veteran actor is renowned for his love of jogging and hiking, and is frequently spotted exercising around the city.

But his latest workout has sparked concern among netizens. According to Hong Kong media reports, a netizen recently saw Chow jogging alone near the Central and Western District Promenade on Hong Kong Island.

While the famously down-to-earth star appeared relaxed and undisturbed as he went about his run, eagle-eyed observers noticed that he was running on the road rather than on a pedestrian pavement or a designated running path.
Online users criticised his choice of route, warning of the dangers of running alongside moving vehicles.
"Running in the middle of the road? That's not a good idea, right?" one commenter asked, while another noted, "This isn't a suitable place for jogging."
Still, not everyone felt Chow was doing anything out of the ordinary, with some fans rushing to his defence. "That's just how things are in Hong Kong. There's no other choice!" one supporter wrote.
Although it remains unclear whether that particular stretch of road was open to traffic at the time or if a proper running path was available nearby, fans' worries are understandable.
After all, Chow has spent years proving that staying active does not have to stop with age—admirers just hope he watches out for the cars.
71418985a8565914: NOVEMBER 11 — Musliha, the cancer patient I had mentioned in a few of my columns, passed away over the weekend.
She died at home, weakened and in pain, after being told there was nothing more the doctors could do for her.
As patients, we were two sides of a coin.
Unlike me, she was married with children.

When she got her diagnosis, the costs terrified her so much she decided not to follow the treatment plan, not realising she still had options funding-wise while I, well, you know what I did after my diagnosis.
It’s been nearly two years since I found out I had cancer and while I’m enduring medically-induced menopause, my cancer is in remission and I don’t have much cause to complain.
For Musliha when she finally returned to the hospital the cancer had advanced and was no longer as curable as it was when she was first diagnosed.
By the time Musliha returned to hospital, the cancer had already advanced incurably. — Photo via Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz website
In her final few months she had been scammed over and over again, by relatives who were jealous of her getting donations, by a fake homestay operator and cheated by a Shopee seller.
She needed diapers not because she was incontinent but because they were the only things that could absorb the constant bleeding from her open wounds.
As the saying goes, there but for the grace of God go I; my outcome was different not because I made better decisions but because of different circumstances.
Musliha deserved to have had someone tell her that she could still have a fighting chance in the early days, that there was zakat, other funds out there, that she didn’t have to run away frightened.
While she has passed, there are still many cancer patients who need help like Nurshazwani who has a little less than RM3,000 to somehow find for her final session of targeted therapy.
You can find a link to her fundraising link here.
In a kinder world, women like her shouldn’t have to sell everything they have to score better odds at beating cancer. But if the world for now can’t be better, we at least can try to be kinder.
May cancer one day pass into the realm of history instead of being a current horrifying reality.
* This is the personal opinion of the columnist.
3d51a7265318ceb4: SYDNEY: Australia recorded a record drop in new home loans in the September quarter as higher borrowing costs and proposed changes to taxes on investment cut demand, another sign interest rate hikes were working to slow the economy.

Wednesday's data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed total new home loans fell 15.5 per cent by value in the September quarter to A$81.16 billion (US$55.6 billion), for a third straight quarter of declines.
The number of loans dropped 15 per cent in the quarter.
Loans for owner occupiers fell 5.3 per cent by value, while those for investment properties dropped a steep 32.3 per cent.
The ABS said the headline drop of 15.5 per cent was the largest quarterly fall since data began in late 2002, driven by investors.
c38ed974b6da0baa: NEW YORK, Nov 11 — Wall Street stocks retreated yesterday, with scandal-hit Nvidia notably tumbling again, while the dollar gained after a hot US inflation report boosted expectations of Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.
After an up day on several Asian and European bourses, Wall Street indices were under pressure throughout the session following US data showing inflation slowed less than expected in October.
The report came hours after Fed Governor Christopher Waller called for a swift response to inflation, suggesting he could even support a 50-basis-point hike in December.
A second Fed official, Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan, also signalled strong support for swift action to address inflation.
“This is a recognition that inflationary pressures continue to accelerate and the Fed is going to have to be aggressive,” said Joe Zidle, chief market strategist, Cresset Capital Management.
All three major indices ended lower, led by the tech-focused Nasdaq which lost 0.7 per cent.
Equity markets also digested some positive developments.

Oil prices continued to retreat on hopes a US-Iran agreement may be closer, while artificial intelligence titan Anthropic disclosed plans to raise up to US$64 billion (RM260 billion) in its upcoming initial public offering, in a listing expected later this month.
Zidle also viewed a silver lining in the plan to hike interest rates in that the market welcomed the Fed’s stance as, ‘We are seeing a problem and we’re on top of it.’”
Fears of a slower AI data centre buildout sparked heavy selling across the tech sector last week, though buyers have stepped back in, with much of Wall Street opening higher yesterday.

But the sector continued to be roiled by Nvidia’s bombshell revelation of an affair between CEO Jensen Huang and a woman reportedly suspected of being a Chinese spy. The AI chip behemoth is now the subject of an FBI investigation.

Nvidia shares fell a further 5.5 per cent after a 4.3 per cent drop Monday. The company slid below Microsoft in market valuation during the session, but ultimately ended back at the world’s second most valuable publicly traded equity after Apple.

The increased AI wariness has taken a toll on Anthropic’s IPO plans, after the maker of artificial intelligence chatbot Claude said it would seek less than the estimated US$100 billion floated just a few weeks ago.
The forecast came in a securities filing in which it revealed that revenue soared to US$17 billion in the third quarter, up from just US$1.4 billion a year earlier.
“The path is not clear for the AI trade, and it may continue to struggle” even if the Anthropic IPO is successful next week, said Kathleen Brooks, research director at the trading platform XTB.
European and Asian stock markets mostly rose.
International benchmark Brent crude oil prices fell below US$90 a barrel for the first time since August but finished at US$91.49 a barrel, down 1.2 per cent.

“President Trump signaling that further strikes on Iran may not be necessary — at a time when oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz are increasing and Middle Eastern exports recover towards pre-war levels — ease supply concerns,” said Axel Rudolph, chief technical analyst at online trading and investing platform IG. — AFP
09d3680273bdcb49: KOTA BHARU, Nov 11 — The Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) is considering extending the duty shifts of its personnel to up to 48 hours in the event of major flooding during the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL), to strengthen its rescue operation capabilities.

Its director, Farhan Sufyan Borhan, said the measure could involve adjustments to the current shift system, from 12-hour rotations to 24- or 48-hour shifts, depending on operational requirements and the situation on the ground during a disaster.
He explained that personnel currently work in three teams on a 12-hour shift system to ensure fire station operations continue around the clock.

“To increase the number of personnel available during major floods, we will manage leave and switch from 12-hour to 24-hour shifts, thereby increasing the number of personnel on duty,” he told Bernama recently.

He added that a freeze on leave could also be imposed, depending on the severity of the disaster, to ensure sufficient manpower, particularly when rescue operations require the deployment of more personnel.

However, Farhan Sufyan stressed that the availability of assets, including boats, trucks and four-wheel-drive vehicles, was equally important to operational effectiveness, as increasing manpower alone would not be sufficient without the necessary equipment.

In a related development, Kelantan JBPM has identified vulnerable groups, including the elderly, persons with disabilities (PwDs) and bedridden patients living in flood-prone areas, to facilitate evacuation efforts in the event of flooding.
He said the exercise was carried out in coordination with the State Disaster Management Committee, involving the Social Welfare Department (JKM) and the Health Department.

He added that information on residents requiring special assistance during evacuation, including the number of elderly people and persons with disabilities in high-risk areas, had been compiled to support operational planning.
“We have identified the number of PwDs and elderly people in these areas who require attention, and the matter has been coordinated at the State Disaster Management Committee level,” he said.
He said the actual evacuation process would depend on prevailing conditions when a disaster occurred, particularly during its initial stages, which were usually challenging for rescue agencies.
He added that training and inter-agency cooperation were also crucial to ensuring the safe and orderly evacuation of vulnerable groups.

Last Sunday, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) issued a caution-level warning for continuous rain in several areas in Kelantan, Pahang and Sabah, as well as throughout Terengganu, effective until today.
MetMalaysia said the affected areas in Kelantan included Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Machang, Bachok, Pasir Puteh, Kuala Krai and Jeli.

Following the warning, the National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre under the Department of Irrigation and Drainage indicated that nine districts in Kelantan could potentially experience flooding during the same period. — Bernama

*Editor’s note: JBPM stands for Jabatan Bomba dan Penyelamat Malaysia in Malay, MTL is short for Monsun Timur Laut (Northeast Monsoon), and JKM is Jabatan Kebajikan Masyarakat (Social Welfare Department).

c950461ae22b9746: NEW YORK: Nvidia shed about US$430 billion in market value over two sessions as new reports deepened questions about CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

The controversy escalated on several fronts on Tuesday as allegations emerged that Huang's relationship with Alice Huang aided at least US$7.5 billion in Nvidia chip shipments to China and that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had previously briefed President Donald Trump on the affair.

Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer demanded answers from the administration and tighter curbs on chip exports to China, while the company's independent directors hired outside counsel to investigate.

The allegations have turned Huang's personal conduct into a broader risk for Nvidia, raising questions about the company's governance and its dependence on the chief executive officer (CEO) who has led it for more than three decades and built it into the dominant supplier of AI chips. He owns about 3.6 per cent of the company — but does not have majority voting control — and runs an unusually flat organisation in which dozens of executives report directly to him.

The FBI is separately examining whether 63-year-old Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Huang has told employees he was unfaithful to his wife but provided no details about the relationship. China's foreign ministry has said the spy accusations are "groundless".
Huang apologised to top executives at a closed-door meeting on Monday before pivoting to business and was back holding meetings at Nvidia's headquarters on Tuesday, CNBC reported.

Nvidia has said its board has no reason to believe US national security or company secrets were compromised and that Huang has committed to cooperating with the internal review. The board has retained Joon Kim, a Wachtell Lipton partner and former acting US Attorney for the Southern District of New York, whose practice includes internal investigations and white-collar defence, to lead the probe.

Nvidia's stock, which had been nearly flat this year before news of the affair broke, has fallen 9.5 per cent since then. The shares have lagged the broader market on investor unease over whether massive spending on AI will deliver adequate returns.
WHEN DID TRUMP KNOW?

The New York Times reported on Tuesday that Rubio had briefed Trump aboard Air Force One en route to China in May about US intelligence indicating Huang was involved with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy. The briefing marked at least the second time in seven months that Trump had been told about the intelligence, the Times reported, citing people with knowledge of the matter.
Trump said on Monday he had spoken with Huang and asked whether he knew the woman was a spy. Trump said Huang told him he had "absolutely no idea" and that he believed the Nvidia CEO.
Trump also said he had not known about the alleged ties when Huang accompanied him to China in May.
A White House official disputed the report and referred Reuters to Trump's comments on Monday.
Schumer said on Tuesday that Congress must have a full accounting of Trump's defence of Huang and called on lawmakers to quickly approve new restrictions on US chip exports to China.
"He's supposed to protect America, not China, not his friends," Schumer said, accusing Trump of failing to address foreign espionage in the American technology industry.
US news publication Axios, citing sources, reported on Tuesday that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick was sent a highly classified memo warning about the Nvidia CEO's relationship with Alice Huang.
Reuters could not immediately verify that report. The Commerce Department and Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside regular business hours.
WHO IS ALICE HUANG?
Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, along with her husband and sister, built a network of companies across China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, The Information reported.

When orders for Nvidia chips subject to US export restrictions stalled, Alice Huang used ties to Nvidia to secure supplies, helping move about 240,000 H100, H200 and some A100 chips into China, according to the report. Some of the chips ultimately served Alibaba, Tencent and smaller Chinese AI labs.
Reuters could not determine Alice Huang's whereabouts to seek comment.

She held senior roles ​at a Shanghai investment firm before becoming the controlling shareholder of Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed International, which was linked to Century Litong, a China-based company that secured preferred cloud partner status with Nvidia in 2023, giving it priority access to the company's chips.

Separately, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday that several US government agencies pushed for Megaspeed to be included on the entity list, a trade blacklist of groups connected to China that US officials say pose national security risks, but the US Commerce Department was delaying efforts to blacklist the company.

The Commerce Department had sought more information about some companies under consideration, the FT reported. It was unclear whether Megaspeed was among those companies, but the delay has left it off the list, according to the report.

The US Department of Commerce and Nvidia did not respond to Reuters requests for comment. Alibaba, Tencent, Megaspeed and Century Litong were not immediately available for comment outside regular business hours. Reuters could not independently verify the reports.

68f3cdd2a507c676: Several members of the Kennedy family, one of America's most famous political dynasties, filed on Tuesday to join a court case aimed at stopping President Donald Trump from building a proposed triumphal arch in Washington, saying it would obstruct views and cast shadows over their relatives' grave sites.

The 250-foot (76-metre) arch, shown in a rendering to include a flame held by a 60-foot gold winged female figure and flanked by gold flying eagles, would be situated across the Potomac River from the Lincoln Memorial on a highway roundabout near the entrance to the Arlington National Cemetery.
A judge has already issued a temporary order blocking construction through Nov 19 as she considers whether to issue a preliminary injunction.

The arch "will permanently cast shadows over and damage historically significant sight lines to the existing grave sites and memorials established in the Kennedy family's honour at Arlington National Cemetery, as well as to the memorials of hundreds of thousands of fallen American heroes," the filing said.

The Kennedy family is one of the most prolific political dynasties in US history, notably including former President John F. Kennedy. Trump's health secretary is Robert F. Kennedy Jr., nephew to the assassinated former president.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Reuters.

The Trump administration contends Congress approved the arch more than 100 years ago when it also authorised construction of a bridge across the Potomac River. It has said that the arch would honour veterans.
Numerous Democrats in Congress have vowed to block construction once they take control in January, after winning November's midterm elections.
4ea40f4dbd3968af: SINGAPORE, Nov 11 — Singapore’s omnichannel media network, SPH Media, said it recently detected cyberattacks on five of its systems, resulting in the exposure of nine per cent of its personal database.
In a statement, the company assured that no payment card details, financial or banking information, or customer account credentials had been compromised.
It said the cyberattacks targeted two groups of systems: those containing personal data and those that did not store any personal data.
“For the first group, the exposed information included predominantly email addresses, as well as some names, mailing addresses, and phone numbers.
“The second group involved unauthorised access to systems that did not contain any personal data,” it said on Tuesday.
SPH Media said it immediately took steps to secure the affected systems and engaged external cybersecurity experts to investigate and contain the breaches.
“We concurrently reported the incident to the Personal Data Protection Commission, Cyber Security Agency of Singapore, Infocomm Media Development Authority and filed a police report.

“We have also informed all impacted parties about the incident and advised them about the precautions they should take,” it said, adding that an advisory has also been posted on its website’s main page. — Bernama
2c8ef4535b81d232: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — A plate hits the table and frankly, it doesn’t look appealing; it’s just a mound of black and white sesame seeds covering a thick brown sauce, with green shoots peeking out from underneath, dotted with golden brown fried crackers.
A closer look at the plate reveals translucent sprigs of jellyfish and those fried crackers are actually Chinese crullers or you tiao.
This is Sotong Paku Pakis, a riff on Sotong Kangkung (cuttlefish salad), which is usually eaten as a snack.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
As they are generous with the thick sauce, it covers everything including the blanched brown cuttlefish. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
Find it at the cavernous Win Kee Food Garden, which houses so many food stalls that you won’t leave hungry.
This stall, called Sotongpaku Kepong, was previously at Sam Gor Kopitiam, Taman Kepong, which consolidated its second stall inside Win Kee Food Garden just a month ago.
Originally started back in 2012, the owner took a 14-year hiatus while overseas and recently revived the stall in the middle of this year.
Its vibe is that of a typical blanched cuttlefish salad, usually found in Chinese and Malay stalls, served as a snack.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Different toppings give varying textures: the jellyfish (left) has a crunchier bite while the ‘sotong’ or brown cuttlefish (right) has a firmer one. – Pictures by Lee Khang Yi
This version is similar to that served at a stall in Gopeng, Perak, which swaps kangkung for paku pakis (wild fern shoots) but the other place serves it with a different sauce.
While kangkung is a cheaper ingredient readily available everywhere, paku pakis has a fresher, tender bite that works better than kangkung, whose hollow stems can sometimes be too fibrous.
Unlike the Sotong Kangkung version, which uses a sweet brown rojak sauce with dried shrimp paste, this version uses a slightly sweet-spicy thick peanut sauce.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Oyster Omelette has firmer egg pieces with oysters that you can order for a more substantial snack. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
It’s generously blanketed with toasted sesame seeds and toasted ground peanuts that boost the flavours even more.

cff231b7ee8d4c12: KOTA BARU: The Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department is considering extending the duty shifts of its personnel to up to 48 hours in the event of major flooding during the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL), to strengthen its rescue operation capabilities.

c3080aa0c902503d: WASHINGTON: Democrats in the US House of Representatives, who will control key committees next year, are preparing investigations into what they say was President Donald Trump's politicisation and gutting of US spy agencies, including whether analysts have censored themselves to avoid retaliation.
"There's absolutely evidence that analysts are hesitant to write on topics that they think might be controversial.

"There's absolutely evidence of a decline in morale in the analytic community because of the pressures that they are under," US Representative Jim Himes, a Connecticut Democrat who will become chairman of the House intelligence committee in January, told Reuters on Tuesday.

There has been little scrutiny of the state of the US intelligence community by the Republican-run Congress during the first two years of Trump's second term, during which the administration fired or forced out hundreds of officers and disrupted the production of analyses on key issues, including Iran.

Himes said that would change after he takes over the committee in January, when Democrats assume control of the House of Representatives and the Senate following their sweep of the November 3 midterm elections.
He did not disclose how the investigations would proceed, but said that one focus would be what he called retaliatory firings.
"We're going to tell the story of the patriots who were fired because they said something that was inconsistent with what the president wanted to be true," Himes said.

Former Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard last year cut her agency's staff by about 40%. CIA Director John Ratcliffe publicly pledged to reduce his workforce by more than 1,000 positions over several years.
Both offered deferred-resignation programmes that provided pay and benefits for employees who chose to leave.

The cuts included the firings of longtime intelligence analysts and officers from top posts, including at the National Intelligence Council, the analytical group overseen by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence.
At least two of those fired were analysts involved in an assessment that contradicted the White House's official policy on Venezuela.

77ce357e31b87614: LONDON, Nov 11 — Michael Carrick drove away from Manchester United’s training ground yesterday with his future hanging in the balance after the latest contentious move by the troubled club’s chaotic hierarchy.
Carrick had awoken to reports that he would be sacked after a torrid start to the season left United languishing in the Premier League relegation zone.
It would be hard for even Carrick’s most ardent fan to complain if the axe fell following United’s worst opening to a campaign for 40 years.

But, in keeping with the muddled thinking that seems to afflict United’s leadership whenever they are faced with a major decision, Carrick got back in his car after yesterday’s training session still none the wiser about his fate.
Rather than put Carrick out of his misery — or hand him an unexpected reprieve — the 45-year-old United boss was left to twist in the wind.
His future will be decided by influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox at a meeting in Monaco today.
Although it is said that no final call has been made, Berrada and Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick.
Ratcliffe and United owners the Glazer family would likely accept that recommendation, plunging the club into yet another managerial crisis.
Weary of their team’s steep decline since their last English title in 2013, United fans could be forgiven for feeling a sense of deja vu.
Just two years ago, Erik ten Hag led United out at Wembley for the 2024 FA Cup final against Manchester City amid intense speculation that he would be sacked regardless of the result.
But United’s shock win forced Ratcliffe to spend weeks debating Ten Hag’s future, including a close-season meeting with Thomas Tuchel in Monaco that ended with the German rejecting the job.
Ten Hag was eventually handed a one-year contract extension prior to the 2024-25 season.
Yet when results dipped at the start of that campaign, he was sacked just three months after being given the new deal.
“They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication. The promises, they didn’t keep,” Ten Hag fumed.
It was a damning indictment of Ratcliffe and his coterie of advisors, including then sporting director Dan Ashworth.
Ashworth’s brief role at United underlined the dysfunction gripping the corridors of power at Old Trafford.
Lured from Newcastle, Ashworth lasted just five months before leaving by mutual consent in 2024, reportedly because he disagreed with the decision to hire Ruben Amorim as Ten Hag’s replacement.
Scorched earth
Perhaps they should have listened because Amorim’s miserable 14-month reign ended acrimoniously in January this year after he warned his bosses to stop interfering.
Carrick stepped into the breach as interim boss and his humble demeanour initially served as a welcome tonic to Amorim’s scorched earth approach.
United qualified for the Champions League, earning Carrick a permanent contract.
But it was a risky move by United’s powerbrokers given the ex-Middlesbrough manager’s lack of coaching experience at the highest level.
Hampered by United’s disappointing transfer window, Carrick came under fire after an embarrassing opening-weekend loss at Hull.
Reports blared that he was certain to be sacked following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth, but United surprisingly granted him a stay of execution.
United finally showed some fight in a dramatic win over Roma last week and a last-ditch draw with Aston Villa on Sunday.
Has Carrick built a siege mentality among his squad that could ease the threat of a first relegation since 1974?
United’s hierarchy seem typically uncertain, postponing their decision until the Monaco summit while pondering who to hire if they do wield the axe.
Former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino is said to have told United he is open to accepting the poisoned chalice despite recently extending his USA contract until 2030.
Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann have also been linked with the 20-time English champions.
But as United defender Lisandro Martinez pointedly said last month: “You can’t keep changing, changing, changing manager? What about other areas?”
Regardless of that warning, Carrick is likely to be fired after one win in 10 league games, while Berrada and Wilcox are believed to be safe.
“I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there,” Carrick unconvincingly said recently.
Until United’s hierarchy muster a coherent vision of their own, the fallen giants will continue to lurch from one crisis to another. — AFP
01b4bc97ea0b24d1: LISBON: Many AI platforms will end up eventually adopting advertising, the head of the online advertising agency Criteo told AFP Tuesday, as investors are focused on whether the technology will ever be profitable.

It has subsequently begun to progressively roll out ads worldwide, in cooperation with Criteo.

OpenAI's rival Anthropic, which is set to imminently go public with a stock listing, has said it doesn't plan to integrate advertising in its AI tools due to data protection concerns as well as to protect the interests of its users.
Microsoft has used ads in its public version of Copilot AI since 2023.
Perplexity has experimented with ads in the US since 2024.
Google is considering integrating ads in Gemini.
Developing AI models and rolling them out requires massive investments.

The rally in AI-related stocks that has buoyed markets this year was testament to investor confidence, but both equity and bond investors have recently grown more wary as inflation and high interest rates are making the endeavour even more expensive.
Criteo works with OpenAI in 89 countries to develop advertising campaigns on AI chatbots.
Komasinski said some 3,600 brands have trialled AI advertising campaigns and they have noted a modest increase in their spending on ChatGPT.
He remains sceptical about AI agents being able to autonomously make purchases.
"It's actually really easy to order unimportant things, and things that are very important you would tend to not delegate to a bot," he said.

89ed138f16a76ee5: NOVEMBER 11 — More than two years ago, I wrote that there is no house arrest under the law in Malaysia.
But a house can be a prison.
If a prisoner is to be under house arrest, the designated house can and must first be declared a prison under Section 3 of the Act.

Section 3 empowers the minister, by notification in the Gazette, to declare “any house, building, enclosure or place, or any part thereof, to be a prison for the purposes of this Act for the imprisonment or detention of persons lawfully in custody and may in like manner declare that any such prison shall cease to be a prison for the purposes of this Act”.

So, when an AFP reporter reported that Malaysia’s former prime minister Najib Razak had left prison for home on Nov 6 after his party said he had paid a RM50 million (S$15.7 million) fine allowing him to serve the rest of his corruption sentence under house arrest, Najib was headed for prison actually.
Albeit his own residence.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A view shows the home of Datuk Seri Najib Razak along Jalan Langgak Duta in Taman Duta, Kuala Lumpur on November 6, 2026. — Picture by Choo Choy May
On the same day Najib was presumed to have headed home, a declaration under Section 3 of the Act was made by the Home Minister and gazetted. The gazette [P.U. (B) 456/2026] reads as follows:

“In exercise of the powers conferred by Section 3 of the Prison Act 1995 [Act537], the Minister declares all buildings and areas measuring 4558.975 square metres at No. 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta, 50480 Kuala Lumpur situated on Lot 5746, Mukim of Kuala Lumpur, District of Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur to be a prison for the purposes of the Act for the imprisonment or detention of persons lawfully in custody.
Dated 6 November 2026
DATUK SERI SAIFUDDIN NASUTION BIN ISMAIL
Minister of Home Affairs”
Read it here.
The declared building is reported as Najib’s residence.
Last night, Najib arrived at his residence in Jalan Langgak Duta to begin serving the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest.

Somewhere in an exclusive and plush area in Kuala Lumpur – that is, Langgak Duta – widely recognised as a sanctuary for Malaysia’s upper-class, wealthy families, business tycoons, and political figures, is a prison.
But a question remains.
If the residence is declared a prison, who’s footing the bill?

0e2a6d2017c353f0: WASHINGTON, Nov 11 — Republicans in the US House of Representatives yesterday blocked an effort to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war, handing President Donald Trump a victory days after his party’s crushing midterm election defeat.

The House voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee, effectively derailing a planned vote today on whether to bring formal charges against the embattled Pentagon chief.
The resolution was introduced by Republican Thomas Massie, a Trump critic who was the only member of his party to oppose the procedural maneuver, according to US media.

The impeachment drive had threatened to deepen Trump’s troubles after Democrats swept last week’s midterms, with anger at the sputtering Iran war and soaring fuel prices helping drive voters to a historic rejection of Republicans.
Republicans still hold a narrow House majority until January, when Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress. And 11 Democrats missed the vote.

Trump hailed the procedural defeat as an “EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot,” in a post on Truth Social, while Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell, in a post on X, called the vote as a “TOTAL VICTORY!”
“We look forward to ending this sham impeachment in the committee room, where facts will continue to prevail and this distraction can be put to rest,” Parnell added.
Hegseth earlier yesterday dismissed the impeachment effort as a “farce” and defended his record leading the Iran war and other military operations under Trump.
“It’s a farce, and it’s a stunt, and everybody knows it,” he said at a Pentagon press conference, branding the accusations “slander” and “sabotage.”
Moments after Hegseth’s televised appearance, Trump signaled his support.
“Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS,” the 80-year-old president wrote on his Truth Social platform.
Vice President JD Vance also backed the defense secretary, saying he had “obviously not” committed impeachable offenses.
‘Would do it again’
Massie’s eight articles of impeachment accused Hegseth of illegally waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief.
Several related to the eight-month Iran war, accusing him of violating the War Powers Resolution, which places limits on US military interventions without congressional authorization.

Other allegations involved the 2025 conflict with Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis and strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, which Massie branded “extrajudicial killings.”
He also accused Hegseth of suppressing free speech by trying to punish Democratic Senator Mark Kelly over a video urging military and intelligence personnel to refuse illegal orders.
Hegseth defended the operations in Yemen, Iran, Venezuela and against alleged drug smugglers, while seeking to equate the impeachment effort with an attack on US troops.
“I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them, and I would do it again tomorrow,” he said.
The decision to send the resolution to committee halts the immediate impeachment drive but does not prevent Democrats from reviving the effort after taking control of Congress in January.
Massie, who lost his Republican primary to a Trump-backed challenger, will leave Congress at the end of his term. — AFP

ee95ce65b404c5f9: PETALING JAYA: Malaysians love a good deal, especially when it comes to food. But when deciding where to eat, the cheapest item on the menu may not be the biggest draw.
A recent nationwide study suggests cleanliness and hygiene rank slightly ahead of affordability, alongside two equally familiar demands: the food has to taste good, and consistency is key.

The research found that 82% of respondents regarded cleanliness and hygiene as important when choosing where to eat, order food or buy beverages. Good taste and consistent quality followed at 81% each, while affordable prices came in slightly lower at 78%.

That hardly means Malaysians have stopped watching their wallets; rather, value appears to be about more than the lowest price. Diners may be prepared to pay a little more when the quality, portion size and overall experience justify it.

Published last month, the study surveyed 1,964 Malaysian adults across Peninsular and East Malaysia between July 3 and 24. The online sample was stratified to reflect Malaysia's population census, although the findings indicate preferences rather than necessarily predicting how people behave in practice.
Home still has a special place
Eating at home remains central to Malaysian life: 62% said they mainly relied on home-cooked or family-prepared meals.
When they did eat out, hawker centres and food courts recorded the highest average visit frequency, followed by mamak restaurants and kopitiams.

Choice also depended on the occasion. Home cooking remained important for routine meals, fast food appealed when convenience mattered, while restaurants and cafés featured more strongly for dates, gatherings and celebrations.

Malaysians also appear reluctant to choose firmly between restaurant chains and independent eateries. While 33% preferred chains and 23% favoured independent establishments, the largest group (44%) had no fixed preference.
Chain diners tended to value familiar menus, consistent quality and trusted brands, while independents appealed more to those seeking better taste and distinctive food.
Younger consumers showed a stronger preference for independent eateries, with 30% of respondents aged 18-24 favouring them compared with 23% nationally.
TikTok has also become a powerful restaurant-discovery tool: 56% of respondents overall used the platform to discover new food and dining options, rising to 72% among those aged 18-24.

Familiarity matters, but Malaysians are hardly unadventurous eaters: 65% said they enjoyed trying new food and beverage trends, while Malay cuisine recorded the highest positive interest at 68%. Western and Thai food also attracted considerable interest.
Health was a further consideration: three-quarters said they tried to choose healthier food and drink options, while 72% watched their intake of sugar, oil or portion sizes.
Among those aged 55 and above, the figure choosing healthier options rose to 88%.

Taken together, the findings suggest Malaysians remain enthusiastic eaters, albeit increasingly demanding ones, too. Cheap food will always have its appeal - but if the table is dirty or the meal disappoints, a low price may no longer be enough.
81cea1d01a7884dd: PETALING JAYA: Today, Bayan Baru is part of everyday life in Penang, its homes, businesses and commercial centres serving a community that grew alongside the state’s industrial expansion.

But half a century ago, Penang was in economic distress. Its traditional trading economy was in decline, thousands of young people were looking for work and the state was struggling to find a way forward.
The loss of its free port status in 1967 had dealt a heavy blow. By the end of the decade, unemployment had reached 16%, creating an urgent need for a new economic direction.
One of the men entrusted with finding it was Chet Singh, who died yesterday aged 90.
As the first general manager of the Penang Development Corporation (PDC), he spent two decades helping turn the late chief minister Dr Lim Chong Eu’s industrial ambitions into reality.
Lim provided the political leadership. Chet and his colleagues were responsible for putting the plan into action, building the machinery that would help transform Penang's economy.
Established in 1969, PDC was tasked with developing labour-intensive industries and attracting foreign investment to a state that could no longer rely on its traditional sources of trade.

Chet took charge as general manager in 1971, aged just 35. He was not a businessman but an administrator, having graduated in economics and history from the University of Malaya in Singapore before joining the ministry of defence in 1960. He became Penang’s state financial officer in 1967.

The challenge was considerable. Penang had to persuade international companies that it could provide the land, workforce and infrastructure needed to support manufacturing on a scale the state had never experienced.
In a 2024 interview with The Edge, Chet recalled that about 50,000 young people were looking for jobs in those early years.
"There was a high rate of unemployment, and E&E jobs would create the necessary jobs in the quickest time," he said, referring to electrical and electronics manufacturing.
The strategy centred on export-oriented industries and free trade zones, where foreign companies could establish production facilities.

But securing investment was not simply a matter of offering land. PDC had to answer technical questions, facilitate operations and convince investors that Penang could support their businesses over the long term.
Chet's account of National Semiconductor's arrival offers a glimpse of how he approached the challenge.

The American company was among the first multinational investors to show interest in Penang. When its representatives arrived with a lengthy technical questionnaire, Chet and the PDC secretary could not answer all the questions immediately.
Rather than bluff their way through, he asked for a day to obtain the information.
He contacted people who could help and returned with the completed questionnaire on Monday afternoon.
The company was impressed and moved into Penang. AMD and Hewlett-Packard followed, while Intel later chose the state for its first manufacturing plant outside the United States.
Those early investments helped establish Penang as an electronics manufacturing centre and connected it to global supply chains.
Much of the work involved ensuring that industrial development could keep pace with investor needs. PDC had to prepare sites and make sure roads, water and electricity were available.
As Chet told The Edge, attracting investors was one thing; ensuring the necessary infrastructure was in place was another.

The corporation's responsibilities also extended beyond the factory gates. During his tenure, PDC undertook the development of several townships, including Bayan Baru, as industrial growth brought more workers and families to the island.
By the time Chet retired in 1991, the scale of the transformation was evident.

A 2019 profile by Perdana.org recorded that the number of companies in PDC's industrial parks had grown from about 200 in 1976 to 300 in 1987 and 500 in 1990. Employment in the parks had reached approximately 115,000.

For thousands of families, these figures represented more than economic growth. They meant jobs for school-leavers, opportunities to acquire new skills and the prospect of building a livelihood without leaving Penang.
Yet Chet was reluctant to take too much credit for what had happened.
He often played down the suggestion that he and Lim had possessed extraordinary foresight.
"People like me and Chong Eu weren’t as far-sighted as many people thought. All we knew was that there were 50,000 youngsters looking for jobs," he said.
It was a candid assessment from a man who had spent 20 years at the centre of the state's industrial transformation.
The immediate problem, as he saw it, was unemployment. The scale of what Penang would eventually become was not something he claimed to have foreseen.

Chet largely kept out of the public eye after retiring, although he returned to serve in a different capacity in 2010, when the Penang government appointed him to a task force to examine ways of improving PDC's performance.

He remained connected to the corporation's work. In July, he visited InvestPenang with his wife, daughter and Penang Skills Development Centre chief executive Hari Narayanan. Staff briefed him on the state's changing industrial landscape and celebrated his 90th birthday.
The visit brought Chet back to an institution he had helped build, though the industrial landscape around him had changed beyond recognition since his early days as an administrator.
“A legend”

Nazir Razak, son of former prime minister Abdul Razak Hussein, paid tribute to Chet, calling him one of the founding fathers of the “Silicon Valley of the East” and saying Penang owed him a great debt of gratitude.

On Tuesday, Nazir posted a photograph of Chet on Instagram, explaining that it had been taken the previous night as the former PDC general manager watched a programme about his father. Chet featured prominently in the programme, and Nazir described him as a legend.
Chet had often acknowledged the role Razak played in Penang’s recovery from the unemployment crisis of the late 1960s and early 1970s.

As prime minister, Razak backed the creation of the state’s free trade zone, despite reservations within the federal government that it could amount to an attempt to restore Penang’s former free port status by another route.
He saw the opportunity to bring foreign manufacturers into the state and used his authority as chairman of the national operations council to push the proposal through.
His backing also carried political significance: Penang was then governed by the opposition, but Razak did not allow that to stand in the way of a plan he believed could revive its economy.
That support helped clear the way for the industrial programme that Lim’s administration and PDC would go on to develop.
Penang's economy has moved far beyond the early factories and assembly lines. But the foundations were laid when the state faced an economic crisis and thousands of young people needed work.

Chet's contribution was made largely outside the political spotlight. He helped build an institution, worked to win the confidence of international investors and ensured that the practical requirements of industrial growth were addressed.

Today, the factories and townships that grew out of that effort are part of Penang's everyday landscape. For generations who have known no other Penang, it may be difficult to imagine how uncertain the future once looked.
His funeral cortege will leave his residence at 24 Changkat Minden, Jalan 5, Minden Heights, at 2.15pm today for the Batu Gantung Crematorium, where the cremation will take place at 3pm.
0f866b7bab22e67f: PETALING JAYA: Bayan Baru hari ini menjadi sebahagian daripada kehidupan seharian di Pulau Pinang, dengan kawasan perumahan, perniagaan dan pusat komersialnya memenuhi keperluan masyarakat yang berkembang seiring dengan perluasan sektor perindustrian negeri itu.

Namun, setengah abad lalu, Pulau Pinang berdepan kemelut ekonomi. Ekonomi perdagangan tradisionalnya semakin merosot, ribuan anak muda mencari pekerjaan dan negeri itu bergelut mencari hala tuju baharu.

Penarikan status pelabuhan bebas pada 1967 memberi tamparan hebat kepada negeri itu. Menjelang penghujung dekad itu, kadar pengangguran mencecah 16%, sekali gus mewujudkan keperluan mendesak untuk mencari hala tuju ekonomi baharu.
Antara individu yang dipertanggungjawabkan untuk mencari jalan keluar ialah Chet Singh, yang meninggal dunia semalam pada usia 90 tahun.

Sebagai pengurus besar pertama Perbadanan Pembangunan Pulau Pinang (PDC), beliau menghabiskan masa selama dua dekad membantu merealisasikan aspirasi perindustrian Ketua Menteri ketika itu, Dr Lim Chong Eu.
Lim menyediakan kepimpinan politik, manakala Chet dan rakan-rakannya bertanggungjawab melaksanakan rancangan itu serta membina jentera yang diperlukan bagi mentransformasikan ekonomi Pulau Pinang.
Ditubuhkan pada 1969, PDC diberi mandat membangunkan industri berintensifkan buruh dan menarik pelaburan asing ke negeri yang tidak lagi boleh bergantung pada sumber perdagangan tradisionalnya.

Chet dilantik sebagai pengurus besar pada 1971 ketika berusia 35 tahun. Beliau bukan ahli perniagaan, sebaliknya seorang pentadbir yang memiliki ijazah dalam bidang ekonomi dan sejarah dari Universiti Malaya di Singapura sebelum menyertai Kementerian Pertahanan pada 1960. Beliau kemudian dilantik sebagai pegawai kewangan negeri Pulau Pinang pada 1967.

Cabaran yang dihadapi bukan kecil. Pulau Pinang perlu meyakinkan syarikat antarabangsa bahawa negeri itu mampu menyediakan tanah, tenaga kerja dan infrastruktur yang diperlukan untuk menyokong kegiatan pembuatan pada skala yang belum pernah dialaminya.
Dalam temu bual dengan The Edge pada 2024, Chet mengimbas kembali bahawa kira-kira 50,000 anak muda sedang mencari pekerjaan pada tahun-tahun awal itu.
"Kadar pengangguran tinggi dan pekerjaan dalam sektor elektrik dan elektronik (E&E) mampu menyediakan peluang pekerjaan yang diperlukan dalam tempoh paling singkat," katanya.
Strategi itu berteraskan industri berorientasikan eksport dan zon perdagangan bebas, yang membolehkan syarikat asing menubuhkan kemudahan pengeluaran.

Namun, menarik pelaburan bukan sekadar menawarkan tanah. PDC perlu menjawab pertanyaan teknikal, memudahkan operasi dan meyakinkan pelabur bahawa Pulau Pinang mampu menyokong perniagaan mereka untuk jangka panjang.
Pengalaman Chet berhubung kemasukan National Semiconductor memberikan gambaran tentang pendekatan beliau dalam menangani cabaran itu.

Syarikat Amerika Syarikat (AS) itu antara syarikat multinasional terawal yang menunjukkan minat untuk melabur di Pulau Pinang. Apabila wakilnya tiba dengan senarai soal selidik teknikal yang panjang, Chet dan setiausaha PDC tidak dapat menjawab semua soalan dengan serta-merta.
Daripada memberikan jawapan yang tidak pasti, beliau meminta tempoh sehari untuk mendapatkan maklumat berkenaan.
Beliau menghubungi beberapa pihak yang boleh membantu dan kembali pada petang Isnin dengan soal selidik yang telah dilengkapkan.

Syarikat itu berpuas hati lalu memulakan operasi di Pulau Pinang. AMD dan Hewlett-Packard menyusul, manakala Intel kemudian memilih negeri itu sebagai lokasi kilang pembuatannya yang pertama di luar AS.
Pelaburan awal itu membantu meletakkan Pulau Pinang sebagai hab pembuatan elektronik dan menghubungkan negeri itu dengan rantaian bekalan global.

Sebahagian besar tugas berkenaan melibatkan usaha memastikan pembangunan perindustrian dapat memenuhi keperluan pelabur. PDC perlu menyediakan tapak perindustrian serta memastikan kemudahan jalan raya, bekalan air dan elektrik tersedia.
Seperti yang diberitahu Chet kepada The Edge, menarik pelabur merupakan satu perkara, manakala memastikan infrastruktur yang diperlukan tersedia merupakan perkara lain.

Tanggungjawab perbadanan itu juga melangkaui kawasan kilang. Sepanjang tempoh perkhidmatannya, PDC melaksanakan pembangunan beberapa bandar baharu, termasuk Bayan Baru, ketika pertumbuhan industri membawa lebih ramai pekerja dan keluarga ke pulau itu.
Menjelang persaraan Chet pada 1991, skala transformasi berkenaan semakin jelas.

Profil oleh Perdana.org pada 2019 merekodkan bahawa jumlah syarikat di taman perindustrian PDC meningkat daripada kira-kira 200 pada 1976 kepada 300 pada 1987 dan 500 pada 1990. Jumlah pekerja di taman perindustrian itu pula mencecah kira-kira 115,000 orang.

Bagi ribuan keluarga, angka itu membawa makna lebih besar daripada sekadar pertumbuhan ekonomi. Ia bermakna peluang pekerjaan untuk lepasan sekolah, peluang memperoleh kemahiran baharu dan prospek membina kehidupan tanpa perlu meninggalkan Pulau Pinang.
Namun, Chet tidak gemar mengambil terlalu banyak pujian atas pencapaian itu.
Beliau sering memperkecilkan tanggapan bahawa beliau dan Lim mempunyai wawasan luar biasa.
"Orang seperti saya dan Chong Eu tidaklah berpandangan jauh seperti yang disangka ramai. Apa yang kami tahu hanyalah terdapat 50,000 anak muda yang sedang mencari pekerjaan," katanya.
Itulah penilaian terus terang daripada seorang lelaki yang menghabiskan masa 20 tahun di tengah-tengah transformasi perindustrian negeri itu.
Menurut pandangan beliau, masalah yang perlu diselesaikan ketika itu ialah pengangguran. Beliau tidak mendakwa mampu menjangkakan sejauh mana Pulau Pinang akan berkembang akhirnya.

Chet menjauhkan diri daripada perhatian umum selepas bersara, namun kembali berkhidmat dalam kapasiti berbeza pada 2010 apabila kerajaan Pulau Pinang melantiknya menganggotai pasukan petugas bagi meneliti cara meningkatkan prestasi PDC.

Beliau terus mengikuti perkembangan kerja perbadanan itu. Pada Julai lalu, beliau mengunjungi InvestPenang bersama isteri, anak perempuan dan Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Pusat Pembangunan Kemahiran Pulau Pinang (PSDC) Hari Narayanan. Kakitangan memberikan taklimat kepadanya mengenai landskap perindustrian negeri yang semakin berubah selain meraikan ulang tahun kelahirannya yang ke-90.

Lawatan itu membawa Chet kembali ke institusi yang pernah dibantunya bangunkan, meskipun landskap perindustrian di sekelilingnya sudah berubah sama sekali berbanding zaman awal beliau berkhidmat sebagai pentadbir.
“Seorang tokoh legenda”

Nazir Razak, anak kepada bekas perdana menteri Abdul Razak Hussein, memberi penghormatan kepada Chet dengan menyifatkannya sebagai antara pengasas 'Lembah Silikon Timur' serta berkata Pulau Pinang amat terhutang budi kepadanya.

Pada Selasa, Nazir memuat naik gambar Chet di Instagram dan menjelaskan bahawa gambar itu dirakam pada malam sebelumnya ketika bekas pengurus besar PDC itu menonton sebuah program mengenai bapanya. Chet mendapat perhatian utama dalam program berkenaan dan Nazir menyifatkannya sebagai seorang tokoh legenda.
Chet sering mengiktiraf peranan Razak dalam membantu memulihkan Pulau Pinang daripada krisis pengangguran yang melanda negeri itu pada penghujung 1960-an dan awal 1970-an.

Sebagai perdana menteri, Razak menyokong penubuhan zon perdagangan bebas negeri itu, meskipun terdapat kebimbangan dalam kerajaan persekutuan bahawa langkah berkenaan mungkin menjadi usaha untuk mengembalikan status pelabuhan bebas Pulau Pinang melalui cara lain.
Beliau melihat peluang untuk membawa pengeluar asing ke negeri itu dan menggunakan kuasanya sebagai pengerusi Majlis Gerakan Negara (Mageran) untuk memastikan cadangan berkenaan dilaksanakan.

Sokongan beliau turut membawa kepentingan politik: Pulau Pinang ketika itu ditadbir pembangkang, namun Razak tidak membiarkan perkara itu menghalang pelaksanaan rancangan yang diyakininya mampu memulihkan ekonomi negeri berkenaan.
Sokongan itu membantu membuka jalan kepada program perindustrian yang kemudiannya dibangunkan oleh pentadbiran Lim dan PDC.

Ekonomi Pulau Pinang kini jauh berkembang melangkaui kilang-kilang awal dan barisan pemasangan. Namun, asas pembangunan itu dibina ketika negeri berkenaan berdepan krisis ekonomi dan ribuan anak muda memerlukan pekerjaan.

Sumbangan Chet sebahagian besarnya dilakukan tanpa mendapat perhatian politik. Beliau membantu membina sebuah institusi, berusaha mendapatkan keyakinan pelabur antarabangsa dan memastikan keperluan praktikal pembangunan perindustrian diberi perhatian.

Hari ini, kilang dan bandar baharu yang berkembang hasil usaha itu menjadi sebahagian daripada landskap kehidupan seharian di Pulau Pinang. Bagi generasi yang tidak pernah mengenali Pulau Pinang dalam keadaan berbeza, mungkin sukar untuk membayangkan betapa tidak menentunya masa depan negeri itu suatu ketika dahulu.
0af2eb3ae116eab1: WASHINGTON: Democrats in the US House of Representatives, who will control key committees next year, are preparing investigations into what they say was President Donald Trump’s politicization and gutting of US spy agencies, including whether analysts have censored themselves to avoid retaliation.

“There's absolutely evidence that analysts are hesitant to write on topics that they think might be controversial. There's absolutely evidence of a decline in morale in the analytic community because of the pressures that they are under,” US Representative Jim Himes, a Connecticut Democrat who will become chairman of the House intelligence committee in January, told Reuters on Tuesday.

There has been little scrutiny of the state of the US intelligence community by the Republican-run Congress during the first two years of Trump’s second term, during which the administration fired or forced out hundreds of officers and disrupted the production of analyses on key issues, including Iran.

Himes said that would change after he takes over the committee in January, when Democrats assume control of the House of Representatives and the Senate following their sweep of the Nov 3 midterm elections.
He did not disclose how the investigations would proceed, but said that one focus would be what he called retaliatory firings.
“We’re going to tell the story of the patriots who were fired because they said something that was inconsistent with what the president wanted to be true,” Himes said.

Former Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard last year cut her agency’s staff by about 40%. CIA Director John Ratcliffe publicly pledged to reduce his workforce by more than 1,000 positions over several years. Both offered deferred-resignation programs that provided pay and benefits for employees who chose to leave.

The cuts included the firings of longtime intelligence analysts and officers from top posts, including at the National Intelligence Council, the analytical group overseen by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence.
At least two of those fired were analysts involved in an assessment that contradicted the White House’s official policy on Venezuela.

The reductions have been viewed inside the intelligence agencies as a continuation of Trump’s campaign against what he called the "deep state,” a move critics say has drained the community of experience and expertise.

Reuters previously reported that some of Gabbard’s projects affiliated with her Director’s Initiative Group, a task force that revisited the 2020 election and the origins of Covid-19, created tensions inside the intelligence community.
That was particularly the case after Gabbard's office revoked the security clearances of current and former intelligence officials a year ago.
Gabbard’s actions caused a breakdown in intelligence sharing and cooperation inside the intelligence community and with Congress, as Reuters previously reported.
“The moment the intelligence community stops telling the truth to national leaders, you get into an Iraq war because of weapons of mass destruction that don't exist,” Himes said.
Himes said he had reviewed a statutorily mandated intelligence community survey showing that, in 2025, the workforce had begun to “feel very real political pressure.”
He added he was working to declassify other internal intelligence community reporting that could potentially underscore the effects of the firings and politicization.
The committee, Himes said, will also probe the administration’s relationships with defense and intelligence contractors and US covert efforts overseas.

418a335b9a2a3e87: PARIS: Lens have sacked coach Yannick Cahuzac less than a week after their 9-1 Champions League defeat at home to Como, a source close to the French club told AFP on Tuesday, confirming a report from sports daily L'Equipe.

Cahuzac, who was appointed by Lens less than two months ago, lost his job after the French Cup winners' humiliating loss to Como last Wednesday, as well as a subsequent 2-1 reversal at their Stade Bollaert-Delelis home against Marseille on Sunday in Ligue 1.

The former Lens captain took over from Dino Toppmoeller in mid-September following the German coach's surprise departure after just four Ligue 1 matchdays.

"In front of our fans, here at Bollaert, this is unacceptable," Lens chairman Joseph Oughourlian told Ligue 1+ on Sunday, adding that he had had the words "never again" painted on the walls of the changing room.
Last season under current Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage, Lens won the French Cup and finished second in the league behind Paris Saint-Germain.

1b1e59572933e14d: Citizens in Gabon went 248 days without access to Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube
Originally published on Global Voices
Image of a smartphone showing the Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, YouTube, and Messenger apps. Screenshot from the DW Afrique YouTube channel.

After more than eight months of government blockage, Gabon has restored its social media access. But it has come at a cost. This reinstatement comes with a tighter regulatory framework and an unprecedented cooperation between the government and various tech giants, raising serious concerns about freedom of expression and privacy.

On February 17, 2026, Gabon’s media regulator, the High Communication Authority (HAC), suspended major social media networks, including Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, “until further notice.” According to the regulator, quoted in the daily newspaper L’Essentiel, this measure targeted not only content “undermining national security” but also content involving defamation, cyberbullying, hate speech, and threats to social cohesion.

At first, the suspension had no real impact, with presidential spokesperson Jennyfer Mélodie Sambat claiming it would solely target Meta platforms. However, according to Gabon Media Time, several influencers, content creators, and citizens later experienced access disruptions on YouTube and TikTok, sometimes rendering connections impossible without a bypass tool, such as a virtual private network (VPN).

The global data platform Internet Society Pulse confirmed this observation, revealing major anomalies for Meta, Telegram, TikTok, and YouTube, but not X (formerly Twitter). The online news portal Le360 Afrique consequently reported a surge in VPN usage in the months that followed.
For 248 days, more than 1.84 million individuals, or 71.9 percent of the country’s population of over 2.5 million, were denied regular access to some of the world’s most popular digital platforms.

On October 24, 2026, the HAC lifted this suspension, with Africanews stressing that this ruling didn’t necessarily mean a return to business as usual. It, therefore, remains to be seen whether Gabon, where Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema has been president since September 2023, will restore digital freedoms or establish a new state-controlled online model instead.
From bypassing the suspension to tighter regulatory frameworks

A new legal framework, enacted on February 26, 2026, underpins this reinstatement. According to Gabon Media Time, Ordinance No. 0011/PR/2026 establishes a regulatory framework for digital platform usage, while Ordinance No. 0013/PR/2026 amends the HAC Reorganization Act.

The HAC also invokes a law, enacted on October 5, that ratifies the social media ordinance and establishes a regulatory framework for AI-generated and AI-amplified content, according to reporting by Gabon Review.

What’s more, available data shows that these regulations have introduced joint liability for those who create and share illegal content and require all social media users to provide personal identification information. Purported as tools to combat abuse, these regulations have raised serious concerns about anonymity, personal data protection, and their stifling effect on public debate.
In a country where criticizing public institutions is politically sensitive, the threat of prosecution for posting online could discourage users from expressing dissent.

The issue here isn’t whether the state should combat cyberbullying, disinformation, or hate speech, but rather how. While these are valid concerns, the real worry is whether its measures are transparent, proportionate, and subject to independent scrutiny.
Tech giants enter the regulatory mix

The most decisive development in this saga was undoubtedly the unprecedented cooperation between the government and Big Tech companies. On July 13, 2026, after a meeting at the AI for Good/WSIS summit in Geneva, Gabonese Minister of Digital Economy Mark-Alexandre Doumba announced an agreement with TikTok. Both parties signed a 12-month cooperation agreement, ensuring the platform’s compliance with Gabon’s new regulatory framework.
At the meeting, TikTok presented its Q1 2026 content moderation results, revealing that it had removed more than 23,500 pieces of sensitive content in Gabon.

Meanwhile, the HAC confirmed that it had established an “active cooperation” with TikTok, Meta, and YouTube to “improve content moderation.” The regulator added that, during the suspension, it also held direct discussions with these companies. However, neither the technical details of these exchanges nor the practical operation of the authorities’ reporting tools has been specified.
Find the HAC spokesperson’s full statement here:

These agreements reflect tech companies’ growing influence in digital platform governance. These platforms are also no longer satisfied with merely hosting exchanges between their users; they now shape decisions about what content remains accessible and what does not.

For governments, partnerships with digital platforms provide a direct channel to deal with content they consider harmful, illegal, or threatening to their regime. For tech companies, complying with the state’s requests and distinguishing legitimate moderation from politically motivated censorship poses a significant challenge.
Cooperation is no substitute for transparency
Working alongside digital platforms isn’t inherently problematic. Tech companies ultimately have a responsibility to deal with credible threats, protect vulnerable users, and enforce their own rules.

However, problems arise when the state has direct access to reporting mechanisms — particularly if the public remains unaware of these partnerships. What criteria determine which content is flagged? How are HAC requests processed? Can users challenge a post removal? Are there any safeguards to protect journalists, activists, and government critics?

The line between harmful content and legitimate political expression is often blurred. Without clear procedures, independent monitoring, and an appeals process, critics say these measures risk becoming tools of influence over public debate.

The situation in Gabon represents a much broader trend. As various African states tighten their grip on digital platforms, tech companies face escalating pressure to comply with new national regulations to maintain key market access. The balance of power between governments and tech giants has ultimately become a defining factor in the future of digital rights.
Beyond Gabon: Who is accountable for digital freedom?
Restoring social media access was imperative for Gabonese citizens, journalists, businesspeople, and content creators alike, all of whom suffered under this suspension.

However, access alone doesn’t guarantee freedom. The real test will be whether internet users can participate in online discussions, criticize public policy, and share information without fear of arbitrary sanctions or disproportionate restrictions.

It also depends on Meta, TikTok, and YouTube demonstrating how their cooperation with the Gabonese government complies with international human rights standards, especially freedom of expression, privacy, and access to information.

The current situation in Gabon illustrates how authoritarian control over the digital sphere evolves. Restrictions don’t necessarily end when platform accessibility is restored. Instead, they become regulatory frameworks, personal identification requirements, and tighter government cooperation with private tech companies.

The challenge, therefore, isn’t just about reconnecting citizens to social media, but also about ensuring the digital spaces they return to remain open to criticism, independent information, and public debate.
Although tech giants can negotiate conditions allowing citizens to regain access to digital platforms, they must also ensure those conditions don’t compromise their fundamental freedoms.

Araghchi called on the UN Security Council to address the potential consequences for international peace and security and hold Washington accountable for unlawful actions.
He also urged Grossi to safeguard confidential information collected during inspections, prevent its misuse for intelligence purposes and bring the matter before the IAEA Board of Governors.

The US state department's Rewards for Justice programme offers financial incentives for information related to threats to US national security.
